issuing_authority: U.S. Department of Homeland Security (signed by the Under Secretary for Management)
geo_constraints: All DHS personnel and components (CBP, ICE, FEMA, TSA, USCIS, Secret Service, CISA, Coast Guard), including Intelligence Community elements

locale_context.region: North America › United States (Department of Homeland Security)
locale_context.regulation: Internal departmental directive · principles plus enumerated prohibited uses
locale_context.culture: US federal agency governance in a security and immigration-enforcement setting: constitutional and civil-rights framing, explicit prohibited uses and human judgment for enforcement, with oversight by Privacy and Civil Rights offices and a public use-case inventory.

key_dates.event: Directive 139-08 signed by Under Secretary for Management Randolph Alles

versions.title: DHS Directive 139-08 Artificial Intelligence Use
versions.summary: Only one version recorded for this policy.
versions.note: Signed January 2025; exact day not stated (the file name suggests 16 January 2025). Supersedes Secretary Mayorkas's August 2023 AI policy statement.

covered_entities: DHS components: CBP, ICE, FEMA, TSA, USCIS, Secret Service, CISA, Coast Guard
covered_systems: AI systems, services, techniques, software and hardware used by or on behalf of DHS
covered_activities: planning, designing, developing, deploying and operating AI
AI use case inventory and risk classification
conditions: High-Impact use cases are subject to minimum risk management practices
face recognition opt-out applies to non-law-enforcement uses
objective: Govern DHS's use of AI across its lifecycle so that it is lawful, mission-enhancing, safe, human-centred and responsibly acquired, and prohibit uses that would violate privacy, civil rights and civil liberties.

related_policies.policy: DHS policy statement on AI acquisition and use (Secretary Mayorkas, August 2023)

conflict_rule: AI use must comply with the Constitution and applicable laws and policies; any use prohibited by applicable law or policy is barred.

sources_consulted: https://www.dhs.gov/sites/default/files/2025-01/25_0116_CIO_DHS-Directive-139-08-508.pdf (cited in the asago file; not consulted)
https://fedscoop.com/dhs-ai-policy-2025-prohibited-uses/ (cited in the asago file; not consulted)
record_provenance.notes: Text taken from the copy in asago-ai/asago-policy-mapper (policy_examples/dhs-gov.md). That file is a third-party markdown summary of DHS Directive 139-08 (with an asago commentary section), not the directive itself, so all clause texts are marked text_is_verbatim=false and wording, section numbering and detail should be checked against the official PDF. Signing month (January 2025) from the summary; exact day unknown. Binding=false: internal directive, mandatory for DHS personnel. It is not verified whether the directive has since been revised or superseded (e.g. after OMB M-25-21, April 2025, whose 'High-Impact' terminology the summary's 2025 inventory section uses); no catalogue link is made because the summary does not say the directive implements it. Use-case inventory figures (158 active use cases) describe the 2025 inventory, not the directive text.

clauses.original_text: Sole-basis enforcement decisions — Relying on AI outputs as the sole basis for determining law enforcement actions (arrests, searches, seizures, citations), civil enforcement actions (fines, injunctions), or denial of government benefits
clauses.action: rely on AI outputs as sole basis
clauses.object: law enforcement, civil enforcement and benefit-denial decisions
clauses.recipient: individuals subject to enforcement or benefit decisions
clauses.requirement: AI outputs may not be the sole basis for enforcement actions or benefit denials
clauses.purpose: human judgment in consequential decisions; due process
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems, services, techniques, software and hardware used by or on behalf of DHS
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text is from the asago markdown summary of Directive 139-08, not the directive's own wording (the summary paraphrases it, partly via FedScoop reporting); marked non-verbatim. Bold labels and list formatting removed.

clauses.original_text: Discriminatory decision-making — Using AI to make or support decisions based on the unlawful or improper consideration of race, ethnicity, gender, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, nationality, medical condition, disability, emotional state, or future behavior predictions
clauses.action: use AI for decisions based on protected characteristics
clauses.requirement: no AI-supported decisions based on unlawful or improper consideration of listed characteristics
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems, services, techniques, software and hardware used by or on behalf of DHS
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text is from the asago markdown summary of Directive 139-08, not the directive's own wording (the summary paraphrases it, partly via FedScoop reporting); marked non-verbatim. Bold labels and list formatting removed.

clauses.original_text: Improper profiling — Improperly profiling, targeting, or discriminating against individuals or entities based on protected characteristics, or in retaliation for exercising constitutional rights
clauses.action: profile, target or discriminate using AI
clauses.requirement: no AI-enabled improper profiling or retaliation for exercise of constitutional rights
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems, services, techniques, software and hardware used by or on behalf of DHS
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text is from the asago markdown summary of Directive 139-08, not the directive's own wording (the summary paraphrases it, partly via FedScoop reporting); marked non-verbatim. Bold labels and list formatting removed.

clauses.original_text: Unlawful mass surveillance — Conducting unlawful or improper systemic, indiscriminate, or large-scale monitoring, surveillance, or tracking of individuals
clauses.object: systemic, indiscriminate or large-scale monitoring or tracking
clauses.requirement: no unlawful or improper AI-enabled mass surveillance
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems, services, techniques, software and hardware used by or on behalf of DHS
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text is from the asago markdown summary of Directive 139-08, not the directive's own wording (the summary paraphrases it, partly via FedScoop reporting); marked non-verbatim. Bold labels and list formatting removed.

clauses.original_text: Unauthorized data sharing — Sharing DHS data or AI outputs with third parties for uses that are prohibited by law or DHS policy
clauses.requirement: no sharing of DHS data or AI outputs for uses prohibited by law or DHS policy
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems, services, techniques, software and hardware used by or on behalf of DHS
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text is from the asago markdown summary of Directive 139-08, not the directive's own wording (the summary paraphrases it, partly via FedScoop reporting); marked non-verbatim. Bold labels and list formatting removed.

clauses.original_text: US citizens must be afforded the right to opt-out of face recognition for non-law-enforcement uses … Face recognition must NOT be used as the sole basis of any law or civil enforcement action
clauses.action: afford opt-out; not use as sole basis
clauses.recipient: US citizens; persons subject to enforcement
clauses.requirement: offer US citizens opt-out of face recognition in non-law-enforcement uses; never use face recognition as sole basis for enforcement
clauses.exception: law enforcement uses (opt-out right not afforded)
clauses.purpose: privacy and civil liberties in biometric identification
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text is from the asago markdown summary of Directive 139-08, not the directive's own wording (the summary paraphrases it, partly via FedScoop reporting); marked non-verbatim. Bold labels and list formatting removed. Two bullets combined.
